text:
sam: Heads-up: we have a reproducible KV-cache correctness regression hitting canary. Some completions include tokens from the previous request in the same worker.
anya: oof. repro? only canary or locally too?
sam: repro locally with the attached small harness. Happens when >64k context + paging enabled and batching churns streams. curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://redwood-canary/api/generate -d '{"input":"A... (65k tokens)"}'
```
logs show stale block reuse:
```
[kv_cache] evict_blocks=12 reuse_hits=3 stale_block_count=2 align_offset=4095
[serve] worker=42 stream=7 returned_token="previous_request:..."
```
miguel: I think this is the off-by-one in the pager that recomputes block alignment when a partially-filled block is evicted. If the tail fragment isn't zeroed, we can end up mapping the wrong kv slice to the new stream.
jessie: I captured a heap/frag profile from the canary machine. Memory grows slowly on long lived workers and fragmentation increases after ~1e6 kv insert ops. Snippet:
```
heap_profile: total=23.1G fragmented=2.7G pages=1728
kv_blocks: active=1484 free=312 fragmented_frag=0.18
```
caroline: failing unit in kv_cache_test::token_alignment_on_page looked like this:
```
assert_eq!(cache.slice(start, len), expected_slice) // got mismatch at offset 4095
```
sam: it only shows up with int8 quantized kernels (A100 qint8 combo). non-quant runs fine. maybe kernel page size interplay.
anya: could be kernel selection timing + batching heuristic that shuffles stream order causing tails to be reused before zeroing.
miguel: quick mitigation: mark paged blocks as "quarantine" for 1 eviction cycle (don't immediately reassign until zeroed). cheap and safe while we root cause. I'll open a PR.
sam: can we add a quick e2e that fuzzes stream order and long contexts? want it in CI guard.
jessie: added a reproducer test to perf-regress harness that runs 1k randomized sequences and checks cross-request contamination. Failing locally ~80% with current canary image.
caroline: unit test also shows a race where align_offset calculation uses stale stream_id when the eviction callback runs asynchronously.
miguel: good catch. my plan: (1) patch eviction to zero tail bytes synchronously, (2) add stream_id check in allocator, (3) quarantine flag for safety. I'll include perf counters for stale_block_count and quarantine_hits.
sam: sounds good. please include a small perf test to prove no latency regression >2% for common 2-4k contexts.
miguel: will do. tagging @deploy-bot to hold new canary until fix merged.
deploy-bot: Canary paused for worker group `kv-paged` pending PR review (auto-paused by policy). :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks everyone. once PR is up I'll smoke on canary and schedule a rollback if needed. :thumbsup:
